candidates.label: Nein
candidates.support: Wikidata's coordinate is corroborated by OpenBible.info's independently recorded point for the same village, about 300 meters apart, and the modern Arabic village name directly preserves the ancient name.

summary.text: Nain was a small Galilean village where, according to Luke 7, Jesus raised a widow's only son from death as his funeral procession left the town.

history.text: The modern village of Nein preserves the ancient name, and a small church commemorating the miracle has stood at the site since at least the Crusader period.

scripture.textWEB: Soon afterwards, he went to a city called Nain. Many of his disciples, along with a great multitude, went with him.

politicalHistory.entity: Kingdom of Herod the Great (ruler: Herod the Great)
Tetrarchy of Galilee and Perea (ruler: Herod Antipas)
Kingdom of Herod Agrippa I (ruler: Herod Agrippa I)

politicalHistory.note: The emperor Nero later added the Galilean towns of Tiberias and Taricheae (identified with Magdala), and Julias in Perea with fourteen villages, to Agrippa II's kingdom; the Jewish historian Josephus dates this to AD 54, but the Jewish Encyclopedia (1906) reads Agrippa II's coinage as pointing to AD 61 instead. These are towns, not land of their own, so this area's extent does not change.

politicalHistory.entity: Roman province of Judea (ruler: Legates, with a legion now based at Jerusalem)
politicalHistory.note: An administrative upgrade (a legate instead of a procurator), not a border or name change.
